title: The New Fama Puzzle
author: Bussière, Chinn, Ferrara, Heipertz
summary: Fama regressions on eight USD pairs: the classic negative slope (high-rate currencies keep appreciating) holds before the 2008 crisis, then disappears and turns positive afterwards.
extracted_hypotheses: Carry profitability in USD pairs is regime-dependent and weakened after 2008
limitations: Abstract and summaries only; full text not read
notes: Directly relevant to H-carry; predicts weaker validation-period carry

title: Carry Trades and Currency Crashes
author: Brunnermeier, Nagel, Pedersen
summary: Carry returns are negatively skewed because positions unwind suddenly when risk appetite and funding liquidity fall; discusses the USD/JPY crash of 7-8 October 1998.
extracted_hypotheses: Carry exposure should be cut when risk (VIX, FX volatility) rises
methodology: Panel of currencies; skewness, VIX, positioning
limitations: Working-paper text; crash timing hard to predict ex ante
contradicting: FX005 (volatility risk explains carry premium rather than offering a timing signal)
notes: Basis for the risk-off filter hypothesis

title: The Dollar and interest-rate differentials: instability near the zero lower bound
author: Engel, Kazakova, Wang, Xiang
url: UNVERIFIED (known only from a search summary; Journal of International Economics 2022)
summary: Evidence that interest differentials predict USD excess returns is unstable over time and disappears when rates are near the zero lower bound.
extracted_hypotheses: Rate-differential signals may fail in Japan's zero-rate years (1999-2022)
limitations: Known only from a search-result summary; full citation and URL to verify before relying on details
notes: Key contradicting evidence for H-carry and H-diffmom

title: Common Risk Factors in Currency Markets
author: Lustig, Roussanov, Verdelhan
summary: A slope factor explains the >5% p.a. spread between high- and low-rate currency portfolios (1983-2007, after bid-ask); evidence is cross-sectional across many currencies.
extracted_hypotheses: Carry premium is compensation for global risk; single pairs capture only part of it
methodology: Portfolio sorts on forward discounts, after bid-ask

title: Carry Trades and Global Foreign Exchange Volatility
author: Menkhoff, Sarno, Schmeling, Schrimpf
summary: High-rate currencies lose when global FX volatility rises unexpectedly; a volatility-risk proxy explains >90% of cross-sectional carry returns.
extracted_hypotheses: Avoid carry exposure in high-volatility regimes
limitations: A risk explanation, not a tested timing rule
notes: Basis for the volatility filter variant

title: What Does the Yield Curve Tell Us About Exchange Rate Predictability?
author: Chen, Tsang
summary: Relative Nelson-Siegel factors (US minus foreign) predict FX 1-24 months ahead, monthly 1985-2005 incl. Japan and the UK: when the US curve shifts down or becomes steeper relative to the foreign one, the USD depreciates 3-4% over subsequent months. Their rolling out-of-sample forecasts do not consistently beat a random walk or a single-maturity differential.
extracted_hypotheses: Relative steepening of the US curve -> short USD/JPY; relative downward shift (falling differential) -> short USD/JPY
methodology: Monthly regressions, Fama-Bliss zero yields; rolling OOS forecasts
limitations: In-sample evidence overlaps our 1990-2014 tuning period; OOS evidence weak by the authors' own account
notes: Sign verified from the text (US = home) before pre-registration

title: The Adaptive Markets Hypothesis: Evidence from the Foreign Exchange Market
author: Neely, Weller, Ulrich
summary: FX filter and moving-average rule profits of the 1970s-80s were genuine but had disappeared by the early 1990s; less-studied rules also declined.
extracted_hypotheses: Do not expect simple price-trend rules to work on USD/JPY after 1990
methodology: Many trading rules, long FX history
notes: Reason no price-trend hypothesis is pre-registered for USD/JPY

title: Currency Momentum Strategies
author: Menkhoff, Sarno, Schmeling, Schrimpf
summary: Cross-sectional currency momentum earns up to 10% p.a. between winners and losers but faces strong limits to arbitrage and is distinct from carry.
extracted_hypotheses: Momentum is a cross-sectional, many-currency effect

title: Carry Trade: The Gains of Diversification
author: Burnside, Eichenbaum, Rebelo
summary: From a single-currency trader's view, diversifying the carry trade across currencies raises the typical Sharpe ratio by over 50%.
extracted_hypotheses: Single-pair carry should be expected to have a markedly lower Sharpe than portfolio carry
methodology: Single-currency vs portfolio carry Sharpe ratios

title: Safe Haven Currencies
author: Ranaldo, Söderlind
summary: The yen and Swiss franc appreciate against the USD when US stocks fall and bond prices and FX volatility rise; strongest for the yen in the 2008 crisis; effects from hours to days.

title: Is Foreign Exchange Intervention Effective? The Japanese Experiences in the 1990s
author: Ito
summary: Using daily intervention data disclosed in 2001, MoF interventions 1991-2001 earned large profits (about 9 trillion yen), leaned against the wind (yen-selling below 125, yen-buying above 125) and were effective in the late 1990s; joint US interventions far stronger.
extracted_hypotheses: Intervention marks policy resistance levels; but the 1990s record was secret until 2001
methodology: Regressions of daily changes on interventions
limitations: Data not observable in real time before 2001
notes: Explains why intervention cannot be a point-in-time trading signal in 1991-2001

title: Is Sterilised Foreign Exchange Intervention Effective After All? An Event Study Approach
author: Fatum, Hutchison
summary: Event study on Japanese daily data: sterilized intervention affects the yen in the short run (under one month), even when secret; largest effects for >$1bn and coordinated operations.
methodology: Event study, sign and matched-sample tests
notes: Supports an event study, not a trading rule

title: Foreign Exchange Intervention Operations (historical data, monthly and quarterly releases)
author: Ministry of Finance, Japan
summary: Official daily intervention records since April 1991 (CSV). Current practice: monthly totals about 2 days after each monthly period, daily detail about 5 weeks after each quarter.
limitations: Start date of monthly publication UNVERIFIED

title: JGB constant-maturity yields, historical (1974-)
author: Ministry of Finance, Japan
summary: Daily JGB yields 1Y-40Y since 1974 (CSV); cross-checked against OECD monthly Japan long rate (corr 0.9995).
limitations: Publication time of day not stated

title: H.10 Foreign Exchange Rates (DEXJPUS via FRED)
author: Federal Reserve Board
summary: Noon New York buying rates, daily since 1971; the project's single USD/JPY price source (Yahoo daily FX bars failed the cross-check).
limitations: One fixing per day (noon ET); no bid/ask

title: CFTC final rules on retail forex (2010): 2% security deposit for major currencies
author: CFTC (as reported by Euromoney)
summary: Maximum 50:1 leverage on major pairs, 20:1 on others; NFA sets the list of majors.

title: OANDA help: minimum trade size (1 unit on v20)
author: OANDA
summary: 1-unit minimum on OANDA's own platform; 0.01 lot (1,000 units) on MT4/MT5. Non-US page.

title: Section 988 vs 1256 treatment of OTC FX (proposed regulations)
author: BDO
summary: Spot FX gains are ordinary (Section 988) unless an election is made; treatment of OTC FX options under 1256 debated.

title: Forex rollover and broker markup (explainer with worked 0.75% markup example)
author: VT Markets / Babypips / Benzinga (secondary)
summary: Rollover = interest differential plus a broker markup, charged at 17:00 NY, tripled on Wednesdays; one worked example uses a 0.75% annual markup.
notes: Used only to set a conservative cost assumption, with 2x/3x sensitivity

title: Third-party reviews of retail USD/JPY spreads
author: compareforexbrokers.com and others
summary: Reviewer tests report about 0.35 pip (raw account, plus commission); no official average spread published by OANDA or FOREX.com for USD/JPY.
notes: Cost assumption set conservatively above these figures

title: Yen carry trade commentary 2024-2026 (BCA, UBS, Amundi)
author: Various
summary: Commentary about 2024-2026 carry unwinds.
notes: Excluded from hypothesis design: post-2023 information must not shape locked research
